channel.desc: For the latest news as it happens ABC News is the home of breaking news, compelling stories and original reporting. Mariam Saab presents the day's top stories and updated news from across Australia and around the globe.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Australian Story
channel.desc: Who cares for our children when we're gone if they can't care for themselves? As Deirdre Croft faces the end of her life, she's on a mission to ensure her son is looked after when she's gone.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC National News
channel.desc: There's never been a more important time for transparency and trust. ABC News brings you today's top stories and latest news, with more reporters to tell you what's going on and why it matters. Presented by Mariam Saab.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Back Roads
channel.desc: Lisa Millar continues her exploration of Shark Bay, a World Heritage listed wilderness on the westernmost point of Western Australia. It's a vivid contrast of turquoise waters and red desert cliffs.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC News Tonight
channel.desc: When you need to know what's happening turn to ABC News for coverage you can trust. Mariam Saab brings you the day's news by reporters in more locations across Australia, connecting communities and telling your stories.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Foreign Correspondent
channel.desc: A revolution is taking place in Indonesia. President Prabowo Subianto is nationalising and militarising the economy to deliver self-reliance. But some warn Indonesia could be returning to the Suharto era.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC Nightly News
channel.desc: More news, more often, with more reporters in more places, connecting communities and telling Australians' stories, plus breaking news and coverage of the issues that matter.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: If You're Listening
channel.desc: Over the next few episodes we take a deep dive into Iran. It's a very complicated country in an even more complicated region. We take a close look at the regime, its history, its problems and what might happen to it next.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC Late News Weekend
channel.desc: When you need to know what's happening turn to ABC News for coverage you can trust. Mariam Saab brings you the day's news by reporters in more locations across Australia, connecting communities and telling your stories.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Expanse: The Nannup Four
channel.desc: A chance encounter in the streets of Melbourne in 1998 leaves a friend wondering what Chantelle McDougall has been pulled into. Is it a cult? Or is her partner Simon Kadwell planning something even worse?

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC Late News
channel.desc: Live across Australia, Mariam Saab brings you the latest news and a roundup of the day's top stories from across Australia and around the globe.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Australian Story
channel.desc: Who cares for our children when we're gone if they can't care for themselves? As Deirdre Croft faces the end of her life, she's on a mission to ensure her son is looked after when she's gone.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC News Overnight
channel.desc: The final word on the top stories, with the latest news and updated information from Australia's most trusted source of independent news. Presented by Mariam Saab.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC National Forum
channel.desc: The first ABC National Forum will focus on the lives and experiences of Jewish Australians, including issues arising from the Bondi terrorist attack. David Speers facilitates a wide-ranging conversation among the audience.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC News Update
channel.desc: The news headlines updating the day's top stories from across Australia and around the world.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Landline
channel.desc: A tasty sampler of stories from the land, covering food, agriculture, crops, climate, business and innovation, and meeting the fascinating people who make rural and regional communities unique. Presented by Pip Courtney.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: DW News
channel.desc: The latest international news and the day's top stories from a European perspective. Our broadcast partner DW brings you live coverage from Berlin with updated reports and expert analysis on the big global issues and events.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Media Watch
channel.desc: The conflict in Iran marks a new chapter in AI-generated war imagery; The Kylie and Jackie O split marks the $200 million collapse of a high-stakes radio gamble; UK Telegraph story on a family struggling to afford 5 holidays.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Asia News Week
channel.desc: Yvonne Yong brings you a weekly roundup of the stories making news across the Asia region, plus what's trending on social media and making an impact on the culture and the way people live.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: DW News
channel.desc: The latest international news and the day's top stories from a European perspective. Our broadcast partner DW brings you live coverage from Berlin with updated reports and expert analysis on the big global issues and events.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Chopsticks or Fork?
channel.desc: New Bo Wa Restaurant in Moree has been around since the 1970s. Ernest and Whitney Lai are the keeping up the tradition of nourishing the community with Aussie Chinese food like prawn cutlets and fried ice cream.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Culture By Design
channel.desc: The final episode introduces audiences to brilliant women designers from across Asia, featuring an architect and graphic designer in Indonesia and ceramicist in India.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: DW News
channel.desc: The latest international news and the day's top stories from a European perspective. Our broadcast partner DW brings you live coverage from Berlin with updated reports and expert analysis on the big global issues and events.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: BTN High
channel.desc: Breaks down the week's biggest news stories for Aussie high-schoolers.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: National Press Club Address
channel.desc: Allegra Spender, the Independent MP for Wentworth, addresses the National Press Club on the topic \.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: The Breakfast Couch
channel.desc: James Glenday, Emma Rebellato, Catherine Murphy and Nate Byrne hear from some of the guests who have appeared on News Breakfast. Plus regulars including our film critic Zak Hepburn and resident foodie Alice Zaslavsky.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC News Update
channel.desc: Start your morning with the latest headlines from ABC News, updating you on the day's top stories and the overnight news from across Australia and around the world.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Landline
channel.desc: A tasty sampler of stories from the land, covering food, agriculture, crops, climate, business and innovation, and meeting the fascinating people who make rural and regional communities unique. Presented by Pip Courtney.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: ABC News Regional
channel.desc: A weekly snapshot of what's going on beyond the big cities and suburbs. From the outback, remote, rural and country towns into the major regional and provincial cities, Olivana Lathouris brings you the best regional stories.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Weekend Breakfast
channel.desc: All the news you need to start your Sunday. Fauziah Ibrahim and Johanna Nicholson bring you the latest news, interviews, politics, culture, weather and global affairs. Plus sport with Jared Coote.

channel.name: ABC News 24 AU
channel.title: Insiders
channel.desc: David Speers and the panel discuss the week in politics including the RBA's next decision on interest rates, the federal budget, plus the Liberals and One Nation face an electoral test at the South Australian State Election.[(96057)]

channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: K-FOOD CLASS
channel.desc: Chef Joseph Lidgerwood?s class is? A Little Too Special! A K-FOOD experience crafted like no other ? Now Open! As global interest in Korean culture continues to thrive, K-FOOD has become one of its most compelling pillars. And today, people aren?t just curious about how it tastes. They want to learn how it?s made. Joseph Lidgerwood, chef-owner of the Michelin two-star restaurant EVETT, is an Australian chef who has developed a deep connection to Korea?s traditional jang and its ingredients. Now, he?s ready to share what he calls the ?the true taste of Korea.? Each episode welcomes a new group of participants from around the world, learning the all-time favorites such as Korean fried chicken, jaeyuk bokkeum, ganjang gejang, godeungeo kimchijjim, and bajirak sujebi, all reimagined through Joseph?s unique style. The atmosphere in the kitchen, shaped by curiosity, focus, and genuine interaction between Joseph and his students, often becomes as memorable as the food they create. You?ll take home the recipes, of course. But what truly sets this class apart is the moments shared along the way, the laughter, the discoveries, and the way flavor bridges cultures. Experience the depth, joy, and creativity of K-FOOD in Joseph?s A Little Too Special: K-FOOD Class!

channel.desc: Simple and Fun Korean Lessons, ?K-Chat: Travel in Korea? What are the most useful expressions visitors to Korea can use right away?From arriving at the airport to finding your hotel and exploring popular travel destinations, this program offers practical expressions for your Korean language journey. It also covers traditional Korean culture and essential travel information, making it an invaluable resource for beginner to intermediate learners! Discover Korean travel expressions in an engaging and entertaining way with skits performed by ONF?s Hyo-jin, Seung-jun, Wyatt, and Alexa. With clear and accessible explanations from Hye-rim of the Wonder Girls, a graduate of Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, you?ll systematically improve your Korean!

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: SMARTBIZ ACCEL 2(10?)
channel.desc: Along with the strengthened manufacturing capabilities of various countries all around the world, \"Smart Factory\" has garnered a lot of attention in the global market. And the government has unveiled and promoted a roadmap \"Manufacturing Innovation 3.0,\" as part of an effort to enhance the competitiveness of the domestic manufacturing sector. Moreover, a domestic major company Samsung Electronics has provided a smart factory solution in order to boost mutual growth with small and medium-sized businesses. SmartBiz Accelerators introduces a variety of domestic small and medium-sized companies that have achieved continuous growth based on the smart factory project provided by Samsung Electronics as well as gives information on the technological competitiveness and the outlook for the companies in the global market. #SmartBizAccelerators #ArirangTV #smartfactory #smartfactoryproject #competitiveness_of_manufacturing #strengthening_competitiveness_of_SMEs #expanding_into_overseas_markets #growth_into_globalbusiness For more information: smartbizacc@arirang.com<!--[data-hwpjson]{ \"documentPr\": { \"di\": \"\", \"dp\": { \"dn\": \"test.hwp\", \"ta\": 1, \"d1\": 5, \"d2\": 1, \"dv\": 0, \"dr\": 1, \"do\": 1, \"vj\": \"1.1\", \"an\": \"Hancom Office Hangul\", \"av\": \"10, 0, 0, 13015\", \"ao\": \"WIN\", \"ab\": \"32\", \"ar\": \"LE\", \"as\": \"Windows_8\" }"text":".

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: DECODED: THE AI CONVERSATIONS
channel.desc: AI is no longer a technology of the future; it is a current reality reshaping our daily lives and entire industries. Korea, in particular, is one of the countries most dynamically experiencing this change, as AI deeply penetrates various sectors, including aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, and manufacturing. Through [Decoded: The AI Conversations], we will examine where this technology is heading and how it is changing our lives and society, together with leaders guiding the Korean AI industry. This journey features Dr. Kang Sung-ju, also known as the science communicator \"Hang sung\", as a fixed panelist. In the conversation among the MC, the panelist, and the guests, complex AI concepts are naturally \"decoded\" into everyday language. This will be a platform that vividly delivers the frontline of AI innovation where technology, industry, and policy intersect.

channel.desc: Nachdem er alle 32 Klaviersonaten von Ludwig van Beethoven aufgenommen hatte, um den 250. Schumann begann das Werk w?hrend seines Aufenthalts in Wien im Jahr 1839 zu komponieren. Die ersten vier S?tze schrieb er dort, den letzten bei seiner R?ckkehr nach Leipzig. Das Werk z?hlt zu den popul?rsten Klavierzyklen des Komponisten. Es besteht aus f?nf S?tzen, die lebhaftes Karnevalstreiben darstellen. Der gefeierte italienische Pianist Riccardo Schwartz (1986) hatte das Privileg, als Solist mit vielen weltbekannten Dirigenten aufzutreten, darunter Gustav Kuhn und Yuri Temirkanov. Zu seinen gefeierten Auftritten z?hlen Rezitals und e f?r Klavier und Orchester in vielen renommierten hallen. Mit dabei: Riccardo Schwartz (Pianist).

channel.name: Classica DE

channel.desc: Der bulgarische Dirigent Pavel Baleff dirigiert das Orchester und den Chor der Op?ra de Limoges in einer Auff?hrung von Anton?n Dvo??ks Rusalka (1900). Rusalka sehnt sich danach, selbst ein Mensch zu werden, um mit dem Prinzen zusammen sein zu k?nnen. Au?erdem, wenn die stumme Rusalka die Liebe eines Menschen nicht gewinnen kann, wird sie ewig verdammt sein. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Mozart ? 3. Violinkonzert: KV. 216
channel.desc: Nr. 3 in G-Dur KV 216 Jedes Jahr wird das Europakonzert von den Berliner Philharmonikern in einem bekannten saal oder an einem besonderen Ort veranstaltet. Das diesj?hrige wird in der pr?chtigen Royal Albert Hall in London aufgef?hrt. Der niederl?ndische Dirigent Bernard Haitink beginnt mit Tschaikowskys Fantasie-Ouvert?re aus "Romeo und Julia". Das "Fr?hlingsopfer" gilt heute als eines der Meisterwerke der klassischen Musikgeschichte und hat viele Komponisten des 20. Jahrhunderts beeinflusst. channel.desc: Die Oper "Mariken in de tuin der lusten" zur Musik von Calliope Tsoupaki basiert auf dem Mysterienspiel Mariken van Nieuwmeghen (c. 1515). ?ber f?nf Jahrhunderte hat diese alte Geschichte nichts von ihrer Kraft verloren und ist fester Teil des Kanons d?nischer Kultur. In dieser Oper folgen wir der neugierigen aber empfindlichen Mariken auf einer Reise durch eine dunkle Welt. Sie trifft auf faszinierende Gesch?pfe wie eine hexenhafte Tante, einen verf?hrerischen Teufel und einen aufdringlichen Papst. Die Ensemble ASKO|Sch?nberg und Tetraktys stehen unter der musikalischen Leitung von Hern?n Schvartzman. Hauptsolisten sind Hannah Hoekstra (Mariken) Harry van der Kamp (Oniel), Jill Feldman (Tankte), Julian Podger (Moenen) und Michael Chance (Papst). channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Waldb?hne 2002 ? Night of the Encores
channel.desc: Mariss Jansons f?hrte die Berliner Philharmoniker auf der Waldb?hne mit ihrem Special Guest Vadim Repin (Violine) durch einen Abend mit beliebten Zugaben und erntete stehenden Applaus. Die Waldb?hne in Berlin ist zweifellos eine der beeindruckendsten Freilichtb?hnen Europas. Jeden Sommer gastieren hier die Berliner Philharmoniker und spielen vor einem Publikum von 20.000 Menschen. Die 2002er Ausgabe dieses es konzentriert sich auf Zugaben, die h?ufig von gro?en Orchestern und Ensembles gespielt werden. Die Berliner Philharmoniker spielen zusammen mit dem in Russland geborenen belgischen Violinisten Vadim Repin, der der j?ngste Gewinner der Queen Elisabeth Music Competition in Br?ssel ist und unter vielen f?hrenden Dirigenten wie Simon Rattle, Valery Gergiev und dieses Mal Mariss Jansons spielte. Das Programm variiert von Wagner bis Tschaikowski und von Sibelius bis John Williams. Die ultimative Zugabe: Paul Linckes "Berliner Luft". Mit dabei: Mariss Jansons Berliner Philharmoniker Vadim Repin.

channel.name: Classica DE

Die Urauff?hrung fand am 3. April 1869 in Kopenhagen, D?nemark, mit Edmund Neupert als Solist statt und wurde mit Begeisterung aufgenommen. Die norwegische Premiere folgte wenige Monate sp?ter. channel.name: Classica DE

Geburtstag von Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827) mit einem au?ergew?hnlichen Projekt: der Aufnahme aller sechzehn Streichquartette des gro?en Komponisten. F?nf Jahre lang widmeten sich die Geiger Pierre Colombet und Gabriel Le Magadure, die Bratschistin Marie Chilemme und der Cellist Rapha?l Merlin intensiv den 650 Seiten von Beethovens Partituren. Ihre Bem?hungen gipfelten in der Auff?hrung des gesamten Repertoires f?r Streichquartett, das drei Jahrzehnte von Beethovens musikalischer Kreativit?t abdeckt, in sechs beeindruckenden en in der Philharmonie de Paris im November 2020. Dieses Programm pr?sentiert Quatuor ?b?ne in der Auff?hrung von Beethovens Streichquartett Nr. 15 in a-Moll, Op. 132, aufgenommen am 24. November 2020 in der Philharmonie de Paris. channel.name: Classica DE
channel.title: Schubert ? Sinfonie Nr. 8 in h-Moll: D. 759
channel.desc: Les Dissonances ist ein K?nstlerkollektiv, das 2004 vom Geiger David Grimal gegr?ndet wurde. Das Ensemble ohne Dirigenten besteht aus Musikern der renommiertesten europ?ischen Orchester, internationalen Solisten und jungen Talenten. In dieser Auff?hrung f?hrt Les Dissonances Franz Schuberts Symphonie Nr. 8 in h-Moll, D. 759, auch bekannt als die 'Unvollendete Symphonie', auf. Schubert begann 1822 mit der Komposition des Werkes, vollendete jedoch nur die ersten beiden S?tze. Der erste Satz, Allegro moderato, hat eine dunkle, geheimnisvolle Stimmung, die einen Kontrast zum sch?nen zweiten Satz in E-Dur, Andante con moto, bildet. Schubert notierte nur ein paar Takte des dritten Satzes, eines Scherzos, in voller Partitur. Es ist nicht bekannt, warum der Komponist seine Symphonie nie vollendete, es gibt jedoch mehrere Theorien. Obwohl das Werk nicht vollst?ndig ist, geh?rt es zu Schuberts beliebtesten Kompositionen. Diese Auff?hrung wurde 2013 in der Cit? de la musique in Paris, Frankreich, aufgenommen. Mit dabei: Les Dissonances.

channel.name: Classica DE

Nasibli entschied sich zwar f?r Jazzgesang, doch ihre Lehrer in Oxford erkannten eine opernhafte Tendenz in ihrer Stimme und rieten ihr zu einer klassischen Ausbildung. Die Solisten sind Sopranistin Eleonora Buratto, Mezzosopranistin Anita Rachvelishvili, Tenor Giorgio Berrugi und Bass Roberto Tagliavini. Als 1868 sein Komponistenkollege Gioachino Rossini starb, schlug Verdi vor, eine "Messa per Rossini" zu dessen Ehren zu komponieren, die von ihm selbst und mehreren anderen italienischen Komponisten geschrieben werden sollte. Verdi schrieb den abschlie?enden Satz, "Libera me". Als die Premiere abgesagt wurde, wurde das Projekt auf Eis gelegt. Als einige Jahre sp?ter der italienische Dichter Alessandro Manzoni verstarb, nahm Verdi seinen Plan wieder auf, ein Requiem zu komponieren ? diesmal zu Ehren des Dichters, den er so sehr bewunderte. Als Opernkomponist wusste Verdi besser als jeder andere, wie man das Werk dramatisch gestaltet, was in der ?berarbeiteten Version seines "Libera me" deutlich wird. Besonders herausragend ist das ber?hmte, kraftvolle "Dies Irae", das die Schrecken des J?ngsten Gerichts darstellt. Johannes Brahms stellte sein Violinkonzert 1878 fertig. Nach Beethovens Violinkonzert ist es das ber?hmteste deutsche Violinkonzert, das je komponiert wurde. Brahms' Violinkonzert wurde 1879 uraufgef?hrt, sein Freund Joseph Joachim, f?r den er das St?ck komponierte. Auch Beethovens Violinkonzert stand auf dem Programm. Beide Werke haben viel gemeinsam, zum Beispiel die Tonart, in der sie komponiert wurden: D-Dur. Verglichen mit anderen ist Brahms' Violinkonzert ein St?ck f?r Virtuosen. Die technischen Anforderungen f?r dieses St?ck sind aufgrund von gebrochenen Akkorden, schnellen Tonleiter-Passagen und rhythmischer Variation sehr hoch. Mit dabei: Itzhak Perlman (Violine).

Obwohl es damals so gut wie ignoriert wurde, entstand ein geb?hrend majest?tisches Werk. Bei diesem wurde auch das 19. Klavierkonzert, KV 459, gespielt. In dieser Folge dirigiert David Zinman die Deutsche Kammerphilharmonie, Solist ist Radu Lupu. Die Aufnahme entstand im Kaisersaal der M?nchner Residenz. Mit dabei: Radu Lupu.

F?nf Jahre lang vertieften sich die Geiger Pierre Colombet und Gabriel Le Magadure, die Bratschistin Marie Chilemme und der Cellist Rapha?l Merlin in Beethovens 650 Seiten Noten. Quatuor ?b?ne erkundete alle Facetten von Beethovens Streichquartettrepertoire: von die jugendlichen Streichquartette Opus 18 bis hin zu den Quartetten Razumovsky, Harp und Serioso (Opus 59, 74 und 95) aus seiner mittleren Schaffensperiode und schlie?lich die Tiefe seiner sp?ten Quartette (Opus 127 bis 135). Seit sich schlie?lich die Metropolitan Opera in New York der epischen Erz?hlung um die Suche nach dem Heiligen Gral annahm, wuchs die Beliebtheit des Werkes stetig an und wurde ?berall auf der Welt aufgef?hrt. Kaum eine Inszenierung von Richard Wagners "Parsifal" wurde jedoch so von Publikum und Kritikern gepriesen wie Nikolas Lehnhoffs Version f?r die Englische Nationaloper von 1999. Opernkritiker des Guardian beschrieben Lehnhoffs Arbeit als "eine der besten Inszenierungen [die sie] jemals gesehen" hatten. Er hauchte der Oper m?hleos neues Leben ein ? und das ohne krampfhafte Innvovationsversuche ? indem er den Nebencharakteren, die h?ufig in Vergessenheit geraten mehr Aufmerksamkeit schenkte. Auf der B?hne des Festspielhauses Baden Baden pr?sentiert das Deutsche Symphonieorchester Berlin 2004 unter der Leitung von Dirigent Kent Nagano Lehnhoffs wunderbare Inszenierung von Parsifal. Die Solisten des Spektakels sind Thomas Hampson (Amfortas), Bjarni Thor Kristinsson (Titurel), Matti Salminen (Gurnemaz), Christopher Ventris (Parsifal), Tom Fox (Klingsor) und Waltraud Meier (Kundry).

channel.desc: Die italienische Dirigentin Speranza Scappucci leitet die Philharmonia Z?rich und den Chor des nhauses Z?rich bei einer Auff?hrung von Gaetano Donizettis tragischer "Lucia di Lammermoor" (1835). Zu den Solisten geh?ren Massimo Cavalletti (Enrico Ashton), Piotr Becza?a (Edgardo di Ravenswood), Andrew Owens (Lord Arturo Bucklaw), Oleg Tsibulko (Raimondo Bidebent), Roswitha Christina M?ller (Alisa) und Iain Milne (Normanno). In dieser Auff?hrung f?hrt Les Dissonances Johannes Brahms' Symphonie Nr. 4 in e-Moll, Op. 98 auf. Brahms vollendete seine letzte Symphonie im Jahr 1885. Er selbst dirigierte die erfolgreiche Premiere im Oktober desselben Jahres in der deutschen Stadt Meiningen. channel.desc: Conrad van Alphen dirigiert Sinfonia Rotterdam in einer Auff?hrung von Pjotr Iljitsch Tschaikowskys Ouvert?ren-Fantasie "Romeo und Julia". Van Alphen gr?ndete Sinfonia Rotterdam im Jahr 2000. Unter seiner passioniert engagierten Leitung hat sich dieses Orchester zu einem der bekanntesten Orchester der Niederlande entwickelt. Tschaikowsky basierte seine Komposition auf Shakespeares ber?hmtem St?ck "Romeo und Julia". channel.desc: Aleeksander Madzar und das Royal Philharmonic Orchestra spielen unter der Leitung von Andre Previn Mozarts 27.Klavierkonzert, KV 595, aufgenommen im Wiener Schloss Sch?nbrunn. Im Jahr 1791, wenige Monate bevor sein kurzes Leben so schmerzvoll und unerwartet zu Ende ging, widmete sich Mozart wieder dem Kompositionsstil, der ihm wohl am ehesten entsprach: das f?r Klavier und Orchester. Man w?rde erwarten, dass unter den schwierigen Umst?nden vor Mozarts Tod ein ernstes und schwerm?tiges letztes Klavierkonzert entstehen w?rde, doch dieses Werk ist ganz und gar positiv und erhebend. Mozart erfreut sein Publikum mit einem gef?hlvollen Kinderlied, das die Freuden der Jugend und des Fr?hlings heraufbeschw?rt. channel.desc: Live from the chapel of the National Shrine of the Divine Mercy in Stockbridge, Massachusetts.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Live Adoration from EWTN Chapel
channel.desc: A brief prayer.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Saints and heroes
channel.desc: Enjoy animated adventures on history's greatest saints, teaching kids faith through their examples.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Adventure Catechism
channel.desc: Learn about God's mercy, and how He provides forgiveness of sins through Confession and Penance.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Hi Lucy
channel.desc: Lucy learns that the only way to the Father is through Jesus Christ.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Rosary For Kids
channel.desc: The Joyful Mystery is highlighted as guardian angel Angelito teaches children.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Savouring Our Faith
channel.desc: Fr. Leo Patalinghug explores the history of St. Joan of Arc at Rouen and then travels to Normandy to honor the brave soldiers who sacrificed their lives for freedom during WWII.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Saint Joseph
channel.desc: Rev Cristian Mendoza reflects on Saint Joseph as the spouse of Mary, chosen as the mother of Jesus, Son of God.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Daily mass
channel.desc: The Holy Sacrifice of the Mass with the friars each day from the EWTN Chapel in Irondale, Alabama. LIVE Monday through Saturday at 8 am Eastern.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: The Holy Rosary from Lourdes
channel.desc: Dedicated travellers join together and pray in a devotional ceremony at the Lourdes Grotto in France.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Praying As A Family
channel.desc: Join these families to see how God stretches out His hand to help and heal those of us who struggle with addictions.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Mother Angelica Live Classics
channel.desc: EWTN foundress Mother Angelica discusses light and darkness, as it relates to the Church.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Real Life Catholic
channel.desc: Chris Stefanick meets Catholic families who are passionate about winemaking.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Lent
channel.desc: Blindness in the Bible is both a physical and spiritual condition.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: Life on the rock
channel.desc: Fr. Mark and the Franciscan Friars of the Eternal Word are back. Interviews, spiritual insights from the friars, music videos and much more.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: The Faithful Traveler In Portugal
channel.desc: See the Portuguese answer to the Croque Monsieur, the Francesinha, at Caf? Santiagom, visit connected Carmelite churches and the view of Igreja dos Clerigos.

channel.name: EWTN UK
channel.title: EWTN Vaticano
channel.desc: Latest news from the Vatican with excerpts and analysis of the Holy Fathers recent audiences and writings, and other featured segments.[(96057)]

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Our Catholic Way Of Life
channel.desc: Fr. Kirby concludes his discussion on Catholicism as a lived way of life by emphasizing the importance of having a relationship with the angels and saints in heaven. (30 minutes).

channel.name: EWTN ZA
channel.title: Way Of The Cross: On The Via Dolorosa
channel.desc: Join the Franciscan Friars and the children from the Christian schools of the Holy Land for the first Friday of Lent on the Via Dolorosa streets in the Old City of Jerusalem. (50 minutes).[(96057)]

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Instruments Of A Beating Heart
channel.desc:
First graders in a Tokyo public elementary school are presented with a challenge for the final semester: performing "Ode to Joy" at the ceremony for the new incoming first graders. Ayame, who often struggles to keep up with the group, is determined to play a major part ? the big drum. We follow Ayame as she experiences shattering blows and joyous victories in the audition process. But to rehearse for the big performance, Ayame must quickly learn to deal with newfound pressure and responsibility. When it comes time to perform in the packed auditorium, will she prevail? Instruments of a Beating Heart intimately examines the Japanese educational system's tenuous balance between self-sacrifice and human growth as it teaches the next generation to become part of Japanese society.

Nominee, 2025 Academy Award, Documentary Short Film
Winner, 2024 IDA Award, Best Short Documentary
Nominee, 2024 St. Louis International Film Festival, Best Documentary Short.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Magical Japanese
channel.desc: The Japanese language is rich in words and expressions influenced by nature, history and culture. This episode looks at words related to the night. In ancient Japan, people appreciated the quiet and darkness of nighttime, and had different names for different times of the evening. The night was also associated with mysterious beings. From his home in Kyoto, poet and literary translator Peter MacMillan guides us through these words and the culture behind them.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: The Seasons Of Yamato
channel.desc: A carpet of canola flowers tells the Yamanobe-no-Michi Road that spring has come. The warm weather tempts tree frogs to come out and ladybugs to play with horsetails. Spring light fills up the field as if to compete with the yellow of the canola flowers. As the sun sets, the yellow of the flowers slowly grows darker until they become black silhouettes. But please do not worry about it. Tomorrow should be warmer than today!\n\n*According to the 24 Solar Terms of Reiwa 4 (2022), Keichitsu is from March 5 to 21.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Core Kyoto
channel.desc: Gold leaf is just 0.1 micron thick, and almost translucent, but it has a lasting luster. Gilt craftsmen utilize its qualities to accent brocade, lacquerware, and Buddhist structures and statues. In the ancient court, a soft and muted finish was favored over glitter and gloss, and this cultivated a Kyoto aesthetic. Today tradition is a stepping stone to new art forms, while gold flakes embellish sake, coffee, and traditional sweets. Discover the gleaming appeal of gold leaf culture in Kyoto.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Core Kyoto
channel.desc: Stone Jizo Buddhist statues dot the streets of Kyoto. In summer, children gather at the street corners where the statues stand for lively Jizo Bon festivities. This event, where people pray for the health and success of their children, is a chance for neighborhoods to strengthen their ties. Discover a cornerstone of ordinary Kyoto faith.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Easy Japanese For Work
channel.desc: This episode is about offering support. To Quang Ngoc-san, from Vietnam, works at an IT company. A new coworker sits next to him, and Ngoc-san wants to help him with any trouble he might have. Ngoc-san originally worked in Hanoi before switching to his current job. His Japanese has improved thanks to the help of his senior, Tobishima-san. From greeting clients to understanding paperwork, Ngoc-san wants to pay forward the kindness he was shown, by becoming a great senior, Senpai, to his new coworker.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Zero Waste Life
channel.desc: Gardener Yamashita Rikito collects plants with nowhere to go?that must be removed for demolition or renovation?and finds them new homes; saving them while saving those who give them up from regret.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: The World Heritage Sites In Japan
channel.desc: Mt. Fuji is Japan's tallest and most famous peak. As an active volcano, it has also inspired awe and terror. Mt. Fuji has also inspired artists, including Katsushika Hokusai, as seen in his famous \"The Great Wave off Kanagawa.\" Many 19th-century prints of Mt. Fuji contributed to Europe's japonisme trend. Explore the beauty of a mountain that inspires both artists and faith.

channel.title: Time Lapse Japan

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Trails To Oishii Tokyo
channel.desc: Bean sprouts are harvested all year and have long been a favorite addition to a healthy diet.
